title: Countable two-layer DG free cover surjective on cocycles
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(A,d_A)$ be an associative unital $\mathbf Z$-graded ring with $d_A:A^i\to A^{i+1}$, $d_A^2=0$, and $d_A(ab)=d_A(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d_A(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module means a graded right $A$-module $M$ with $d_M:M^j\to M^{j+1}$, $d_M^2=0$, and $d_M(ma)=d_M(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d_A(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Cohomology is $H^i(M)=\ker(d_M:M^i\to M^{i+1})/\operatorname{im}(d_M:M^{i-1}\to M^i)$; a quasi-isomorphism is a DG module map inducing isomorphisms on all these groups. Countable means countable in the sense of [def-sfb-countable-set]. Assume the set $\coprod_i A^i$ is countable. Let $M$ be a right differential graded $A$-module such that $\coprod_i M^i$ is countable. There exist a DG module map $\pi:Q\to M$, disjoint countable sets $U,V$, integers $t_w$ for $w\in U\amalg V$, and a homogeneous graded right $A$-basis $(e_w)_{w\in U\amalg V}$ of $Q$, with $|e_w|=t_w$, such that $\pi:Q^k\to M^k$ and $\ker(d_Q:Q^k\to Q^{k+1})\to\ker(d_M:M^k\to M^{k+1})$ are surjective for every $k$. For $u\in U$ one has $d_Q(e_u)=0$, and for $v\in V$ one has $d_Q(e_v)\in\bigoplus_{u\in U}e_uA$. In particular $\coprod_i Q^i$ is countable, $Q_U=\bigoplus_{u\in U}e_uA$ is a DG submodule, and the inclusion $Q_U\hookrightarrow Q$ splits as a graded module map; $Q_U$ and $Q/Q_U$ are direct sums of shifts of $A$ as DG modules.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, statement and proof, with the countability refinement invoked in Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1).

proof.text: Put $E=\coprod_{k\in\mathbf Z}M^k$ and $Z=\{(k,z)\in E:d_Mz=0\}$. For each $(k,m)\in E$ take distinct symbols $x_{k,m},y_{k,m}$ in degrees $k,k+1$, and for each $(k,z)\in Z$ take a symbol $s_{k,z}$ of degree $k$. Let $V$ be the set of $x$ symbols and $U$ the set of $y$ and $s$ symbols, with their displayed degrees $t_w$. These are disjoint countable sets: restrict the given injection $E\to\mathbf N$ to $Z$, and encode the three symbol types by $3c,3c+1,3c+2$. Define $Q^n=\bigoplus_{w\in U\amalg V}A^{n-t_w}$, explicitly the finite-support families of coefficients in the indicated additive groups. Addition is coordinatewise; the right action is $(e_wa)b=e_w(ab)$, extended additively. Associativity and the unit law follow on each coordinate from those of $A$. Thus the formal $e_w$ form a homogeneous graded right $A$-basis.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof; countable refinement in Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1).

proof.text:
Define an additive degree-one map $D$ on finite sums by
$$D(e_wa)=\delta_wa+(-1)^{t_w}e_wd_Aa,\qquad \delta_{x_{k,m}}=e_{y_{k,m}},\quad\delta_y=\delta_s=0.$$
The formula is well-defined because coefficients have unique coordinates, $d_A$ is additive, and finite sums remain finite; its terms have degree $t_w+|a|+1$. The Leibniz identity on a coordinate follows by expanding $d_A(ab)$:
$$D(e_wab)=\delta_wab+(-1)^{t_w}e_wd_A(a)b+(-1)^{t_w+|a|}e_wa\,d_A(b)=D(e_wa)b+(-1)^{t_w+|a|}e_wa\,d_A(b).$$
It extends to homogeneous finite sums by additivity. Also $d_A(1)=0$, since applying the Leibniz identity to $1\cdot1$ gives $d_A(1)=d_A(1)+d_A(1)$. Hence $D(e_w)=\delta_w$.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof; countable refinement in Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1).

proof.text:
For a $y$ or $s$ symbol, $D^2(e_wa)=e_wd_A^2(a)=0$. For $w=x_{k,m}$, expand twice to get
$$D^2(e_wa)=(-1)^{k+1}e_{y_{k,m}}d_Aa+(-1)^ke_{y_{k,m}}d_Aa+e_wd_A^2a=0.$$
Here $D(e_y)=0$ and $|y|=k+1$ are used. Additivity gives $D^2=0$ on every $Q^n$. Therefore $d_Q=D$ makes the constructed graded module a DG module, and $d_Q(e_u)=0$, $d_Q(e_v)\in\bigoplus_{u\in U}e_uA$ hold exactly as asserted.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof; countable refinement in Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1).

proof.text:
Define $p_x=m$, $p_y=d_Mm$ for the symbols indexed by $(k,m)$, and $p_s=z$ for the symbol indexed by $(k,z)$. Set $\pi(\sum_we_wa_w)=\sum_wp_wa_w$. This is an additive degree-zero right $A$-module map by the associativity and distributivity axioms. The three assignments satisfy $d_Mp_w=\pi(\delta_w)$: for $x$ this is the definition of $p_y$, for $y$ it is $d_M^2m=0$, and for $s$ it is the defining equation of $Z$. The module Leibniz identity then gives
$$d_M(p_wa)=\pi(\delta_w)a+(-1)^{t_w}p_wd_Aa=\pi D(e_wa).$$
Summing proves that $\pi$ is a DG module map.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof; countable refinement in Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1).

proof.text: For every $m\in M^k$, the element $e_{x_{k,m}}\in Q^k$ maps to $m$, proving degreewise surjectivity. For every $z\in\ker(d_M:M^k\to M^{k+1})$, the element $e_{s_{k,z}}$ has degree $k$, differential zero, and image $z$. Hence the restriction of $\pi$ to cocycles is surjective in every degree. This uses actual cocycles, not merely representatives of cohomology classes.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof; countable refinement in Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1).

proof.text: Here is the countability check for the entire homogeneous disjoint union. Fix injections of $U\amalg V$ and $\coprod_i A^i$ into $\mathbf N$. For $r\in\mathbf N$ let $T_r\subseteq\coprod_nQ^n$ consist of elements with at most $r$ nonzero coordinates. A member is determined by its degree $n$ and its list of nonzero coordinate/coefficient pairs sorted by the injective coordinate labels. For each fixed list length at most $r$, these are finitely many natural-number labels; encode them by iterating the injective pairing $(a,b)\mapsto 2^a(2b+1)-1$, also recording the length and the degree (encode $n\geq0$ by $2n$ and $n<0$ by $-2n-1$). This gives an injection $T_r\to\mathbf N$; injectivity of the pairing follows by removing the unique power of $2$ from its value plus $1$. The cited countable-union statement now applies to $\bigcup_{r\in\mathbf N}T_r=\coprod_nQ^n$. Thus $Q$ is countable. Only finite lists occur, not an infinite product.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof; countable refinement in Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1).

proof.text: The coordinate submodule $Q_U=\bigoplus_{u\in U}e_uA$ is stable under $D$, since $D(e_ua)=(-1)^{t_u}e_ud_Aa$. The coordinate projection that kills all $x$ symbols and fixes $y,s$ is a graded right $A$-linear retraction of $Q_U\hookrightarrow Q$. The quotient has basis the classes $\bar e_v$, $v\in V$, and its differential is $D(\bar e_va)=(-1)^{t_v}\bar e_vd_Aa$, because $\delta_v$ lies in $Q_U$. A generator in degree $t$ with this differential is a copy of $A[-t]$: explicitly $A[-t]^n=A^{n-t}$, $d_{A[-t]}=(-1)^td_A$, with unchanged right action. The maps $a\mapsto e_ua$ and $a\mapsto\bar e_va$ therefore identify $Q_U$ and $Q/Q_U$, respectively, with the indicated direct sums of shifts, including their differentials. No DG splitting of $Q$ is asserted.

The statement is unchanged and keeps the right-module Leibniz convention of the source. The countability hypothesis on A matches 0CRM, and no other hypothesis is added. Step-by-step checks: the D formula has the right degree and satisfies Leibniz; d_A(1)=0 is proved explicitly; in D^2 on x the terms (-1)^{k+1} and (-1)^k cancel; pi commutes with d because d_M p_w=pi(delta_w) for x, y and s; the s generators give cocycle lifts; the finite-support encoding into N is injective and the union over T_r is all of the disjoint union of the Q^n, as the sequence clause of lem-trf-countable-unions needs; Q_U is D-stable, has a graded (not DG) retraction, and Q_U and Q/Q_U are DG-isomorphic to sums of A[-t] with differential (-1)^t d_A. Edge cases M=0, A=0, negative degrees and nonzero d_A all hold. On duplicates, the lem-pc free-complex-cover nodes are the special case of ordinary complexes over a ring and lem-sfb-dg-property-p-resolution has no cocycle surjection or countability, so neither duplicates the item. There are no new nodes. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-countable-unions is a status-mathlib set-theoretic leaf (countable unions) with no proof closure. Neither assumption gives it and it is not a step of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proofs, so it is accepted. There is no SGA citation.
